Converts a number or a text to a UByte, an 8-bit integer from 0 to 255. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals only know `Int` and `Float`. A whole number that is too large or below 0 keeps its lowest 8 bits (`UByte(-1)` is 255), a real is rounded to the nearest whole number (halves go to the even one) and stops at 0 or 255 if it is outside. Use [SatUByte](SatUByte) to stop whole numbers at 0 and 255 as well.

```blitzbasic
;run
Print UByte(200)
Print UByte(-1)
Print UByte(256)
Print UByte(300.0)
```

```text
200
255
0
255
```
@param value  A number or a text with a number in it. A text may start with `$`, `0x`, `%` or `0b` for hexadecimal or binary digits.
@returns The UByte.
@gap Not in the originals, which have no integers of other sizes.
